newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-TORRANCE PULLS OUT OF PLAYERS' CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TORRANCE PULLS OUT OF PLAYERS' CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Injury-prone Sam Torrance had to pull out of the European Tournament Players' Championship (TPC) shortly before the start on Thursday.
The 43-year-old veteran of the last eight Ryder Cups for Europe pulled a muscle in his neck getting out of bed on Wednesday.

He tried to go through his practice routine before playing the first round on Thursday morning but could not swing properly and had to withdraw without going to the tee. He had spent much of Wednesday undergoing intense physiotherapy treatment.
Torrance has had several minor injuries over the past year and has suffered numerous mishaps in his career, including the 1993 Ryder Cup when he missed the singles because of an infected toe.
This year's campaign has been no exception and the Scot has only just got back to 12th in the Ryder Cup points table, having held a promising position at the end of last year.
Torrance is the second British withdrawal in 48 hours, European number one Colin Montgomerie having pulled out on Tuesday for unspecified personal reasons.
